question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral and PQ is a diameter of the circle. If ∠RPQ = 23°, then what is the measure of ∠PSR?
solution:
Given:

PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral and PQ is the diameter of the circle. 

∠RPQ = 23°

Concept used:

In the case of a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles of the quadrilateral is 180°.

The sum of all internal angles of a triangle is 180°.

The angle subtended by a diameter on any point of a circle is 90°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b7829eed107f7fa2f0fc7fc931337168a2b25f09a12992165fff21b95d1a168.png] 

According to the concept, ∠PRQ = 90°

Considering ΔPRQ,

∠RPQ + ∠RQP + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 23° + ∠RQP + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠RQP = 180° - 113°

⇒ ∠RQP = 67°

Since the circle is circumscribed on a quadrilateral PQRS, PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral.

So, ∠RQP + ∠PSR = 180°

⇒ 67° + ∠PSR = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 180° - 67°

⇒ ∠PSR = 113°

**∴ The measure of ∠PSR is 113°.**
